newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 97 sugar output about 1.8 mln T -analyst.
newsitem.headline: Polish 97 sugar output about 1.8 mln T -analyst.

text.p: Polish sugar production in the coming 1997 season will be about 1.8 million tonnes and by 2000 average annual production will be about 1.9 million tonnes, a study by an Agriculture Economy Institute (IER) analyst showed.

"Under normal weather conditions in 1997...the harvests will total about 14.2 million tonnes of beets, with sugar production of about 1.8 million tonnes," Zygmunt Smolenski of the government-linked IER said on Tuesday.
The forecast, delivered at a food industry conference in Warsaw, assumed that average yields will be 350 quintals of beets per hectare, and the average sugar content will be about 12.8 percent.
In 1996 sugar production rose to a record of 2.3 million tonnes, from 1.58 million tonnes in 1995, while beet harvests were 17.5 million tonnes last year and 13.3 million the previous year.

Smolenski said that by the year 2000 average annual production would rise to 1.9 million tonnes with harvests of 15 million tonnes, with average yields of 370 quintals per hectare and sugar content of 12.9 percent.
He said in his report that the rise in output would be due to in part to better production techniques.
